name: Simone de Beauvoir
role: French philosopher, novelist and feminist theorist (1908–1986)
summary: Simone de Beauvoir, an existentialist philosopher and author of The Second Sex, argued that womanhood is made by society and that women's liberation requires economic independence and an end to male domination in marriage, family and work. She sided with the left against capitalism, accepted concretely justified violence against oppression, campaigned for legal abortion and against torture in Algeria, and from the 1970s was an active feminist who refused wages for housework.

notes: First audit (revised after integrator review). Read by theme: The Prime of Life (Spain, Munich, Occupation and Resistance passages), the Declaration of the 121 as reported by Barrat, the Russell Tribunal verdicts, The Second Sex (unabridged, local library; conclusion, marriage, abortion, prostitution, religion and independent-woman chapters), The Ethics of Ambiguity (chapters 1-4), her 1976 interviews with Gerassi and Schwarzer, the Stanford Encyclopedia entry, and the Bardot essay. Change of view: before the 1970s she held that a socialist revolution would solve the woman question and opposed an autonomous women's movement; from 1972 she declared herself a feminist and in 1976 said the socialist countries had not achieved real socialism and that class and sex contradictions are equally essential; her mature position is the later one. Not found or not searched: her essays Pyrrhus and Cineas, An Eye for an Eye and Must We Burn Sade? (no copy opened), The Long March, America Day by Day, Force of Circumstance, The Coming of Age and her 1977 Le Monde petition, so her record on the death penalty, prostitution law, homosexuality and age of consent stays null. Prostitution: The Second Sex says it will disappear only when every woman has a decent job and customs allow free love, and calls repressive measures hypocritical, which does not settle whether sex work should be legal. Themes thin: government, world and economy statements beyond class and capitalism.
